# Run book: Browse users and roles

[Run books](README.md) | [User guide](../user-guide/browse-users-and-roles.md) | [Spec](../specs/browse-users-and-roles.md)

## Contents

- [Purpose](#purpose)

- [Verify](#verify)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

## Purpose

Answer "why can this person do that" without opening the Keycloak console; the screen is read-only.

## Preconditions

- Sign-in is configured and the signed-in user holds the identity.read right.
- The Keycloak service account has the view-users and view-realm roles.

## Verify

Automatically: `npx playwright test e2e/journeys.spec.ts -g "Browse users and roles"` (add `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8088` to run against the compose stack).

By hand, in the example web application at `/identity/directory`:

1. **Read the user table.** Each user shows their realm roles and the rights the role translation grants. Expect: The user ann is listed with the editor role and the docs.read right.
2. **Read the role table.** The role table shows what each role grants, including roles that grant nothing. Expect: The viewer role is listed with no rights.

## Troubleshooting

**Table 1 — Known problems**

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The screen shows 403 | Your token has no role that maps to identity.read | Ask for a role that is translated to identity.read |
| The screen shows 500 or 401 from Keycloak | The service account is missing or lacks view-users | Give the client the realm-management view-users and view-realm roles |

Related framework features: OoBDev.Keycloak (`KeycloakDirectoryReader`); OoBDev.AspNetCore.Abstractions (`IRoleRightMapper`).
